thread:
maya (PM): quick heads-up — Q2 prioritization deck is live. I put up RICE scores for the top 6 initiatives; can the eng + data folks sanity-check before the all-hands?

maya (PM): high-level ask: we need to decide whether to prioritize Dedicated autoscaling improvements (lower latency variance for sustained workloads) or Private KMS/HSM integration (sales blocker for 2 enterprise deals). both are high impact but very different effort/confidence profiles.

alex (ENG): looking. my initial read: autoscaling perf looks medium effort (3 sprints across runtime + infra), KMS/HSM is high effort due to compliance and onboarding (5-7 sprints plus security review). also KMS needs partner legal + infra changes.

maya (PM): thanks. my RICE numbers currently:
R (reach)= 6 for autoscale, 4 for KMS; I (impact)= 7 autoscale, 8 KMS; C (confidence)= 60% autoscale, 50% KMS; E (effort in 'person-months') = 4 autoscale, 10 KMS. gives autoscale = (6*7*0.6)/4 = 6.3, KMS = (4*8*0.5)/10 = 1.6.

jordan (Data): can we sanity-check reach? Reach for KMS should probably be higher for enterprise ARR — sales told us 2 deals immediately, pipeline 10 more. if reach is measured in customers impacted within 6 months, KMS might be 3 or 4, not 4? need definition.

maya (PM): good point. right now reach is "# of customers expected to convert / directly enable in 6 months". we can revisit to include pipeline weighting but want to keep RICE consistent.

priya (AE): sales feedback: two active proofs are blocked; conversion impact per deal is ~200k ARR. If we count revenue-weighted reach, KMS jumps a lot. but that's not how we've been scoring.

sam (SRE): also consider sequencing: autoscaling reduces cost spikes and SLO incidents — immediate ops win. KMS is a gating factor for net-new large customers. We could do a smaller MVP for KMS (bring-your-own-key via proxy) to reduce effort.

alex (ENG): agree on KMS MVP idea. minimal surface: expose a KMS integration shim + config + audit logs. no HSM initially. I estimate MVP effort 6 person-months vs full 10. if we set E=6, KMS RICE becomes (4*8*0.5)/6 = 2.67 — still lower than autoscale but closer.

maya (PM): flag: our Q2 capacity for new cross-team projects is ~8 dev-months if we want to keep near-term reliability work manageable. so choosing KMS full would block other ops work.

jordan (Data): quick data check — last quarter, 12% of API token spend came from enterprise customers (top 10), they contribute 48% of revenue. If pipeline converts, KMS could materially move MRR. Suggest we add a qualitative "strategic" multiplier outside RICE for enterprise land-and-expand.

maya (PM): hmm — adding multipliers breaks comparability. But we can add a separate "strategic value" note. For the RICE-based shortlist we should keep consistent scoring, then annotate strategic flags.

priya (AE): that works. sales will accept an MVP KMS timeline if we get clear SLO and a commit to full integration in next quarter pending pipeline movement.

sam (SRE): technical constraints: autoscale change requires runtime batching logic changes + canary testing on Dedicated fleet. Risk of transient higher latencies during rollout. Need rollout criteria: 99th p50/p95 stable for 3 days, perf regression <5% average.

alex (ENG): putting rollout criteria here to be explicit:
```
- Canary on 10% of Dedicated capacity for 7 days
- No increase >5% in p95 latency
- No increase in error rate >0.1% above baseline
- Auto rollback on sustained regression for 1 hour
```

maya (PM): perfect. for KMS MVP rollout criteria: support KMIP-compatible keys, end-to-end encrypted key transit, audit events to console, and PM-signed security signoff.

jordan (Data): also recommend we quantify confidence: autoscale confidence = 70% (we have perf prototypes), KMS MVP confidence = 55% (lots of external dependencies).

maya (PM): updated table in the deck accordingly. I also added an impact vs effort scatter plot. current quick ordering by RICE: autoscale, observable cost tooling, embeddings cache, KMS-MVP, streaming improvements, reranker tuning.

priya (AE): can we deprioritize reranker tuning this quarter? customers asking but it's lower ARR impact. sales prefers KMS then embeddings cache.

alex (ENG): reranker tuning is low effort and can be paired with an engineer's on-call bandwidth — we can squeeze small experiments without full project allocation. keep as low priority but do a spike.

maya (PM): decision needed: do we commit Q2 capacity to autoscale (4 pm) + small reranker spike (1 pm) + observability infra (3 pm) — that fits 8pm budget. Alternatively, KMS-MVP (6 pm) + observability (2 pm) + reranker spike — also fits but less ops cover. votes?

alex (ENG): vote autoscale + observability + reranker spike. ops fragility is my main worry.

sam (SRE): vote autoscale.

priya (AE): vote KMS-MVP (but will accept autoscale if leadership decides).

jordan (Data): abstain; need final numbers in deck to model ARR scenarios.

maya (PM): noted votes. I'll update RICE numbers with adjusted effort/confidence and add a strategic-flag appendix. planning sync 10:30 tomorrow to lock Q2. planner-bot will post the updated deck link here.

planner-bot: Updated roadmap deck: https://redwood.example.com/q2-roadmap (version 2) :spiral_calendar: 

maya (PM): thanks — please review before 10:30. if you have alternate scoring logic (e.g., revenue-weighted reach), paste a quick calc in thread so I can include it in the appendix. :thumbsup:
